rspec_bulk_generate_ai_summaries_job_spe.note: All 9 failures share one pre-existing root cause: the spec calls/stubs `job_instance.on_complete` as an instance method, but `BulkGenerateAiSummariesJob` defines `on_complete` only via the job-iteration DSL block (`on_complete do...end`, production line 100), which is NOT an instance method; rspec verify_partial_doubles raises 'does not implement #on_complete'. The feature diff touches NEITHER the production `on_complete` block NOR these spec examples (confirmed: `git diff develop...HEAD` contains no `on_complete`). The feature's OWN 2 new examples ('marks the claim row :failed when validation fails', 'zero-criteria job batch ... marks every claim row :failed and still fires the failure completion notification') PASS. Matches the orchestrator-provided known pre-existing set (broken at develop base).

rspec_consumer_specs.note: Ran the specs that consume the modified shared code (generate_ai_summary_with_credit_flow funnel guard, the validators). The single failure — GenerateAiJobApplicationSummaryJob 'broadcasts failed status when the pipeline raises' (spec line 233) — is PRE-EXISTING and NOT a feature regression. The test stubs `generate_ai_summary_with_credit_flow` to raise BEFORE any AiJobApplicationSummary is created; the analog job's own private `broadcast_completion` then hits `return unless ai_job_application_summary` (no summary record) and skips the broadcast, so the expected failed broadcast never fires. The feature's change to that method is fully stubbed out; `git diff develop HEAD` for both `app/jobs/generate_ai_job_application_summary_job.rb` and its spec is EMPTY (byte-identical to develop, no branch commits touched them), so it fails identically at develop base. Deterministic (fails in isolation and as a single example — not flaky).
